To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2} & \ge 5x \\ -2{x}^{2}-5x & \ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-2{x}^{2}-5x$ lies above the $x$-axis or touches this axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-2{x}^{2}-5x & =0 \\ -x(2x+5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=-\frac{5}{2}$ and $x=0,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/33b031b579d84d633e4dcc56c912333327449fcbc6969eeceb34e209c4d308d1.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-2{x}^{2}-5x\ge 0,
$$

 we look for the part of the parabola that is above the $x$-axis or touches this axis.

 Based on the graph, the solution is $-\frac{5}{2}\le x\le 0.$ 

Using interval notation, we write $x\in [-\frac{5}{2},0].$
